## 📰 In-Depth: 2026 Global Digital Economy Conference OPC Special

### Haidian Showcases 30+ OPC Startups at the “Global OPC Co-Creation Festival”

On July 2, the 2026 Global Digital Economy Conference opened at the Beijing National Convention Center. With the theme *“Building a Digital-Friendly City — Smart Benefits Without Borders, Digital Connects the World”*, the conference launched the first-ever **“Global OPC Co-Creation Festival.”** Haidian District brought 30+ OPC startups to the expo, with the slogan *“Come to Haidian, where one person’s dream can have a world-class stage”* drawing widespread attention.

**✨ Featured Projects:**

- **NeZha Interactive** — “Dragon Bone Animation”: Founder Su Kui single-handedly built a platform that generates 2D skeletal animation from a single sentence. Won first prize in the OPC category of “Entrepreneurship Beijing.”
- **ZeroTech** — “AI Sleep Companion”: Full sleep-cycle coverage with AIGC sleep music + health monitoring, creating a direct-to-user software-hardware content ecosystem.
- **Sheet Music Conversion Tool** — A folk music enthusiast used vision LLMs to reduce hours of work to 1 minute.
- **Industrial AI Brain** — A materials science PhD back from overseas signed nearly ¥30M in orders.
- **“Head Star” OPC Community** — Located in Zhongguancun Sci-Fi Industry Innovation Center in Shijingshan District, providing computing vouchers, full-stack AI tools, and office space.

The event features 24 workshops, 35 startup roadshows, 50+ OPC creator showcases, 50+ keynotes & panels, 100+ booths, and a ¥140K prize pool.

### Beijing Hosts First “Global OPC Co-Creation Festival”

The festival connects AI creators, developers, startup teams, industry partners, investors, and real application scenarios into one open, co-creative AI marketplace. Shi Haotian, a PhD candidate from Fudan University’s China Research Institute, showcased his OPC business on site, stating, *“Thanks to rapid AI development and strong government support for innovation, OPC has entered its golden age.”*

## 🏛 Policy Radar: Accelerating Local Government Support

### Chongqing: Exclusive AI OPC Support Policy

On June 29, at the 10th “Yu Chuang Yu Xin” Entrepreneurship Competition finals, the Chongqing Human Resources and Social Security Bureau officially unveiled its AI OPC startup support policy. It targets three core pain points — insufficient startup capital, high technical dependency, and difficulty acquiring orders — with a comprehensive “Five Linkages” approach:

**💰 Funding Matrix:**

- **Individual loan guarantee:** Up to ¥500K, 50% interest subsidy, max 0.5%/year guarantee fee subsidy
- **SME loan guarantee:** Up to ¥6M
- **One-time startup subsidy:** Up to ¥8,000
- **Startup launch fund:** ¥10K–¥50K

**🏗 Incubation Infrastructure:**

- New OPC startup ecology communities with integrated computing power, AI tool development, and order matching
- Zero-rent co-working spaces and low-cost offices

**🎓 Skills Training:**

- Up to ¥1,500 entrepreneurship training subsidy + ¥6,000 vocational skills training subsidy
- Innovative “OPC Night School” covering AI apps, content creation, and business management

**🛎 Service Guarantee:**

- “One-Stop OPC Startup” service: online business registration, social insurance, and subsidy applications
- Qualified AI OPC talent eligible for Chongqing Talent Card

**Nan’an District Response:** Plans to build 20 offline OPC communities with 3,000 dedicated workspaces.

## 📈 Industry Trends: AI Agents Reshaping the Startup Paradigm

### The “Digital Employee” Era for OPC Has Arrived

A viral deep analysis — *“The Advanced and Fragile Nature of OPC Business Models in the AI Agent Era”* — systematically examines OPC opportunities and risks:

**✅ Advantages:**

- AI Agents evolve from instruction-executing tools to autonomous planning, tool-calling, cross-system collaboration “digital employees”
- One person + a few Agents = complete business loop: customer service Agent → contract draft Agent → marketing Agent
- Decision chain shortened from months (in large enterprises) to minutes
- Zero office politics, zero approval friction: 80% of energy goes into value creation

**⚠️ Vulnerabilities:**

- “Always-on” trap: AI runs 24/7, humans lose the right to “go offline”
- Single point of failure: no team backup, no institutional buffers
- “Efficiency trap”: over-relying on AI for known tasks weakens ability to handle novel situations
- Personal brand as double-edged sword: brand = personal reputation, one mistake can destroy years of work
- No cross-disciplinary “knowledge spillover” — risk of intellectual rigidity

### How One OPC Achieved ¥5M Annual Revenue with 17 AI Agents

OPC Network reported a case study of an entrepreneur running 17 AI Agents who reached ¥5M annual revenue after one year. The core methodology: systematically map high-frequency business processes to individual AI Agents, orchestrating specialized Agents to collaborate — one person delivering what used to require a 10-person team. “Agent orchestration” is becoming the superpower of the super-individual.

### OPC in E-Commerce

The real face of 2026 e-commerce entrepreneurship: one person, one computer, a few Agents. Investors are now funding AI-driven micro-startup teams (1–3 people) with monthly costs under ¥20K, achieving output that used to require 10-person teams. One person handles product sourcing, operations, design, and customer service — AI redefines what “one person can do.”

## ⚡ Risk Disclaimer

- **Single-entity fragility**: OPC lacks organizational redundancy — weaker risk resistance than traditional firms
- **“Always-on” burnout risk**: AI Agents’ 24/7 capability can erode work-life boundaries
- **Platform dependency risk**: tying core processes to a single AI platform creates supply risk
- **Personal brand = business lifeline**: one reputation crisis can destroy years of brand equity
- **Technology churn**: rapid AI tool iteration demands continuous learning
